flashcards.definition: Father of Histology who defined 21 primary tissue types without microscope.
First animal phylum in evolution to exhibit true tissue-level grade of organization.
Flattened pavement endothelium lining blood vessels and alveolar air sacs.
Plastic distensible compound epithelium with umbrella cells lining urinary bladder.
Tight junctions seal fluid barriers; Gap junctions pass ions/signals between cells.
Fibroblasts synthesize matrix/collagen; Mast cells release histamine/heparin/serotonin.
White fat is monolocular energy storage; Brown fat is multilocular UCP-1 heat generator.
Haversian canal surrounded by concentric lamellae, lacunae with osteocytes, and canaliculi.
Skeletal muscle is voluntary, striated, syncytial; Smooth muscle is involuntary, unstriated, fusiform.
Junctional complexes with fascia adherens, desmosomes, and gap junctions for cardiac syncytium.
I-band and H-zone shorten, Z-lines approximate, while A-band length remains constant.
Clumps of RER and free ribosomes synthesizing protein in cyton and dendrites; absent in axon.
Star-shaped CNS glia forming perivascular end-feet surrounding brain capillaries.
Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; Schwann cells form PNS myelin.
Fast impulse conduction leaping from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier in myelinated axons.
